prompt: Review an unseen sanitized MLOps or LLMOps platform and release packet. Defend the user contract, immutable release identity, evaluation, registry and promotion controls, batch or online serving choice, request path, GPU and runtime capacity, gateway policy, canary and rollback, drift response, telemetry, security/privacy and unit economics. Recover one reviewer-injected bad-model, latency or cost incident, prove the bounded user outcome independently, and revise the design after a material hardware, model, data, tenant, latency, safety, residency or budget constraint changes.
deliverables: User operation, SLI/SLO, error budget, harm, abstention, fallback, non-model baseline and explicit non-goals.
Immutable release manifest joining source, pipeline, dataset/labels/features, model/tokenizer, prompt/retrieval/policy, image/runtime and evaluation/approval identities.
Registry object, immutable artifact, mutable alias, promotion authority, audit and exact running-version proof.
Representative chronological evaluation for classic ML or nondeterministic LLM behavior with critical slices, uncertainty, evaluator versions and error costs.
Justified batch, synchronous, asynchronous or streaming serving mode and complete request/state path.
Gateway authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, quota, rate, concurrency, token, route, retry and deadline contracts.
GPU discovery, placement, profile, topology, weights, workspace, KV cache, batching, memory and health capacity model.
Queue, admission, cancellation, TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput and head-of-line evidence.
Shadow/canary cohort design, exposure math, minimum evidence, quality/safety/SLO/cost gates, promotion, kill switch and compatible rollback.
Data, feature, concept, behavior, calibration, system-performance and cost drift classification with label-delay treatment.
Telemetry schema/version, trace correlation, sampling, content redaction, retention, access and cardinality budget.
Incident timeline, reversible containment, preserved lineage, recovery and outcome proof, prevention, changed-constraint defense and exact cleanup.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies unfamiliar synthetic release manifests, artifacts, evaluation results, registry history, routes, workloads, hardware profiles, traces, costs and outcome labels.
No real credential, customer data, shared production service, unrestricted cluster or GPU administration, external model endpoint, unbounded traffic or unknown cleanup.
Every claim binds request, tenant, release, immutable artifact and relevant event/deployment times.
Mutable aliases are recorded as decisions but never substitute for resolved versions and digests.
Evaluation data, scorer and configuration are versioned; leakage, slice coverage, uncertainty and nondeterminism are addressed.
Allocated hardware is separated from usable memory, scheduler state, runtime saturation and useful throughput.
Canary rates use exposure denominators and predeclared gates; health checks alone cannot promote.
Retries share one end-to-end deadline and do not repeat billable or externally visible effects blindly.
Drift alarms cannot authorize retraining or promotion without classified evidence and normal release controls.
Sensitive inputs, outputs, prompts, retrieval context, embeddings, labels and traces have explicit lifecycle and access controls.
Reviewer observes injected-incident recovery, changed-constraint revision, independent user postconditions, delayed recall and cleanup.
